post.caption: This tiara was a wedding gift twice. The Girls of Great Britain and Ireland gave it in 1893. The bride was Mary of Teck, who married on July 6. Lady Greville led the committee, and it bought the tiara from Garrard. Leftover money, at Mary's request, went to HMS Victoria widows and orphans. Diamond festoons and scrolls were once topped with large pearls, and in 1914, Mary swapped the pearls for diamonds. In 1947, now Queen Mary, she gave it to her granddaughter Elizabeth. It was a wedding present, and Elizabeth's first tiara. It is reportedly nicknamed Granny's Tiara, and Elizabeth II is shown wearing it on banknotes and coins.
